channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: UK House Prices Remain Under Pressure as Mortgage Costs Rise
item.description: The UK housing market faces “significant” tests from higher borrowing costs and fears of tax rises in next month’s budget, estate agents warned.
item.dc:creator: Irina Anghel

item.title: Kirk: Tariffs Are Taxes on US Businesses and Families
item.description: Ron Kirk, former US Trade Representative and former Dallas mayor, says tariffs amount to taxes on American businesses and families and warns small businesses and manufacturers will bear the cost of the trade fight. Kirk says the integrated North American economy makes the US, Canada, and Mexico stronger and argues China is the real economic competitor. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Julie Fine on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Agather: More Texas Stock Exchange Announcements Coming
item.description: Elaine Agather, Global Vice Chair of JPMorgan Private Bank and Chairman of the Dallas Region for JPMorgan Chase & Co, says more Texas Stock Exchange announcements are expected next week. Agather says Texas is becoming an extension of Wall Street as more capital and companies move into the state. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Julie Fine on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dr. Oz: Fraud Findings Could Double Medicare Trust Fund Life
item.description: Dr. Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, says more than $20 billion identified by the Treasury Department in suspected health care fraud and money laundering could double the life of the Medicare trust fund. Dr. Oz also says more drug pricing deals are in the works and calls on Congress to codify the administration’s most favored nation pricing agreements. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Administration Working on More Drug Pricing Deals, Oz Says
item.description: The Trump administration is pursuing additional drug pricing deals with pharmaceutical companies, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Mehmet Oz told Bloomberg Television.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Cohrs Zhang

item.title: BRICS 2026: What to Know About the Summit, Member States, Tensions With Trump
item.description: BRICS — an acronym that stands for Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa — has morphed from a term conceived by a Wall Street economist into a club of nations that accounts for around a quarter of the world’s nominal gross domestic product and roughly half of its population. It now has 10 full members, bringing together some of the globe’s biggest energy producers and consumers.
item.dc:creator: Mike Cohen

item.title: Apple Unveils Foldable iPhone & New AI Strategy
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are T. Rowe Price Portfolio Manager Tony Wang, IDC Senior Director, Data & Analytics Nabila Popal, Former Apple CEO John Sculley, Signet Jewelers CEO J.K. Symancyk, LightShed Partners Walter Piecyk, S&P Dow Jones Indices CEO Catherine Clay, Oak Hill Advisors Founder & CEO Glenn August, QTS Co-CEO Tag Greason, AGCO Corp. CEO, Chairman & President Eric Hansotia, & Unifor National President Lana Payne. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Energy Secretary Wright on Fuel Prices, Iran and Venezuela Production
item.description: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the surge in fuel prices is being driven less by crude itself than by a shortage of refining capacity. Speaking on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition," Wright also says the Trump administration intends to expand US refining capacity and expects gasoline prices to ease in the coming weeks, though he calls diesel a bigger challenge. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Unveils New Products Under Ternus | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 9/9/2026
item.description: Apple unveiled a new lineup of products Wednesday, including a foldable iPhone, the company's first product launch under its new CEO John Ternus. Bloomberg Intelligence's Mandeep Singh and Bloomberg Tech Host Ed Ludlow discuss the new iPhone Duo and what the announcement says about Ternus' leadership. Then, Economist and Financial Insyght President Peter Atwater, who coined the phrase 'K-Shaped Economy', reacts to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said it's now a 'C-Shaped' economy. Finally, Michael Conrath, JPMorgan Asset Management Chief Retirement Strategist updates us on what workers in the back half of their careers should be looking at in their portfolios as they prepare for retirement. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas Makes Trump the Closing Argument
item.description: The president is making the November election all about himself.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Supreme Court Again Asked to Weigh In on Missouri Voting Map
item.description: An anti-gerrymandering group has asked the US Supreme Court to prevent Missouri from utilizing a new voting map that favors Republicans during the November election to determine control of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Republican Midterm Convention 2026: Live Coverage of Trump Speech, GOP in Dallas
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Appeals Court Denies Bid to Block Missouri GOP-Backed Voter Map
item.description: A federal appeals court denied an anti-gerrymandering group’s bid to prevent Missouri from utilizing a new voting map that favors Republicans during the November election to determine control of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Independent Voters Ready to Vote GOP Out, Says Wendy Davis
item.description: Former Texas State Senator Wendy Davis said that polling shows that independent voters are 'ready to vote the GOP out' in Texas. Davis, a Democrat, said that in order for her party to win a Senate seat in Texas, candidate James Talarico needs to keep offering solutions and stay disciplined on messaging. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: GOP Pushing for Paxton to Win in Texas
item.description: Ray Washburne, the co-chair of the Republican midterm convention, said he expects Trump's super PAC, which has already given $10 million to Ken Paxton's Senate campaign in Texas, 'is going to come in with more money.' He speaks on "Balance of Power" from Dallas. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Air Force One Slide Accidentally Deployed, Delaying Trump Trip
item.description: President Donald Trump’s departure for his midterm convention in Dallas was delayed by an unexpected culprit: the emergency slide on the Qatari-gifted jet used as Air Force One.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason and Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Republican Midterm Convention Kicks Off | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 9/9/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz is in Dallas for the Republican midterm convention. On today's show, convention co-chair Ray Washburne, Lone Star Project Founder Matt Angle, Republican Strategist Vinny Minchillo and US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lula Cuts Fuel Taxes as Oil Prices Rise Ahead of Election
item.description: Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced additional cuts to fuel taxes in a bid to shield consumers from the impact of surging oil prices just weeks before the country’s presidential election.
item.dc:creator: Martha Beck and Rafaela Duarte

item.title: Republican Washburne Downplays Affordability Concerns
item.description: Ray Washburne, co-chair of the host committee for this week’s Republican convention in Dallas, said President Donald Trump and the GOP will have no problems generating enthusiasm at the party’s midterm event by stressing the strength of the economy.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter

item.title: Missouri Voting Map in Doubt After US Judge Revives GOP Plan
item.description: A federal judge cast new doubt on which congressional map Missouri will use in the November election by reviving one that would favor GOP candidates, shortly after the US Supreme Court rebuffed a bid by state Republicans to block an alternative map pushed by Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg
